title.title: A counterexample to Griffiths' positivity conjecture
title.subtitle: Claim: rank-2 bundles $E_m$ on $\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1$ that are ample but carry no Griffiths-positive metric

plain: Two ways to say a bundle is 'positive', by algebra and by curvature, were believed equal; here they differ

panels.caption: all ample; for $m \ge m_0$ none has a Griffiths-positive metric

beats.text: Pull one bundle $G$ back by higher and higher power maps
A curvature obstruction at a point eventually rules out every positive metric

steps: Pull one bundle back by the m-th power map, for larger and larger m
But curvature piles up at a point: past some m, no positive metric

achievement.label: Griffiths' positivity question (1969)
statement: E \text{ ample} \;\Longrightarrow\; E \text{ has a Griffiths-positive metric}
achievement.context: Before: true for line bundles and on curves; widely believed true in general
achievement.note: $m_0$ comes from a compactness argument and is not explicit

verify.detail: Lean states it with custom definitions of ampleness and Hermitian metrics, which need an audit
verify.ourCheck: We did not read the 181-line challenge file in full

voice.text: Griffiths asked if ample bundles always carry positively curved metrics. True for line bundles.
Pull back by higher and higher power maps; ampleness lasts, but curvature eventually fails.
Claimed: ample bundles with no positive metric.

sources.quote: E_m = f_m^*G ⊗ O(1,1) (f_m = m-th power map) is ample for all m ≥ 1 but admits no smooth Hermitian metric with strictly Griffiths-positive curvature for all m ≥ m0 (m0 ineffective)
Griffiths (1969, 'Hermitian differential geometry, Chern classes and positive vector bundles', Problem 0.9)
